questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have always had a dream of going to Canada, so being able to combine both academic and experiencing a new culture was a perfect. One of the reason for choosing Canada was its nature and the active lifestyle surrounding the campus and the city that I lived in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
As I was traveling during covid-19 there were a lot of extra restrictions and regulations that I had to pay attention to, this made it way more difficult to find the necessary information as they basically changed every week. 
Other than that I thought it was quite easy to find the relevant information and our contact person in Canada was really great at helping out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any due to covid. We were supposed to have a meet and greet during the first week, but weren't allowed to gather that many people cause of covid. This could have been really helpful as I had a few questions regarding daily life on campus and such.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were a few different options. You could either choose to live in a single room, single connected room, single suite and a four bedroom suite. I lived in a four bedroom suite with 3 roommates from 3 different countries (Russia, Singapore and Mauritius)

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my apartment we had a shared kitchen where we could all cook as we wanted. A meal plan was available if you wanted, by wasn't mandatory in my apartment where in some of the other apartment a meal plan was mandatory (they had no kitchen)

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Most of the students living on campus are quite young (I was 26 when I was on exchange) and if you decide to live in a four bedroom you are most likely gonna be living with people from different cultures, which mean they are gonna be doing stuff differently. This is both a big part of experiencing other cultures, but can be hard in the beginning to get used to. Other than cooking is a bit difficult as you won't have any kitchen utensils unless you buy it all or have a roommate who has bought it and is willing to share. This made cooking for me very difficult as I didn't wanna spend the money buying all the utensils, but only the bare necessities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I would fill out online form with my top 10 courses at my host university and then my contact person would sign me up for those courses that had free spaces. Don't worry if you don't get the courses you want. During the first 2 weeks of the semester you can drop in and out of courses and a lot of courses will be available by then and then you can just register for them yourself during those 2 weeks.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Your contact person can help you out with all the questions that you have.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100%. I got in to all the classes that I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for everything even though you don't have pre-req needed for the class. The professors are really excited to have exchange students, so just apply for everything. GO ask your contact person, she can "hack" you into all courses that you want, and if there's room for it, she/he will do it, at least they did with me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general the level of the courses wasn't super high. I followed two second year classes, 1 third and 1 fourth year. All of them was doable and the workload per class isn't as high as at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In all of my classes I did not have a textbook and all teaching was done via powerpoints. I really missed having a textbook as I personally like to read about the subjects rather than just listening.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HES 201 - Exercise Prescription
HES 203 - Lifespan Physical and Motor Development 
HES 380 - Exercise Metabolism 
HES 488 - Cortical Control of Movement

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you find metabolism interesting I would definitely recommend taking HES 380. The prof Jonathan is really great at explaining the stuff and puts all his time and effort into you getting as big as outcome as possible.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't call the unexpected but I had to buy a lot of outdoor/hiking clothing as I wanted to do a lot of hiking.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is a bit more expensive than Denmark, but on the other hand going out is a bit cheaper (Restaurant, cinema, bar etc.)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a ton of options, some were shut down due to covid but most were up and running.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join one of the intramural leagues if you're into sport, this can be (Football, volleyball, dodgeball etc.) or join VOCO which is the outdoor club and through that you can borrow all outdoor equipment you need for going on a trip on your own.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Banff and Jasper. Rent a car if you can and just go for a long ride to either of those 2 cities. The icefield parkway road going from Banff to Jasper is spectacular.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy. Canada is not that different from Denmark tbh. Get used to saying "how are you" and "i'm fine" whenever you step into a shop, meet people or whatever. They say it everywhere as a greeting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend classes, live in shared accommodations and join clubs.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Small talking. Canadians are really great at small talking.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Ask for help. There are a lot of ressources for you to use, you just gotta use them. 
If you want a course, apply for it even though you do not meet the pre-requisites. 
You only need 3 courses to be a fulltime student (At least I did). I found it hard to accept this fact, because most other student have either 4 to 6 classes per semester. But that just gives you more time for social events.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find a friend with a car. It can be hard to get around if you're not just going downtown but want to go out for hikes and other stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet a lot of new people and improving my english.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Covid-19.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
